name: Interactive High Resolution Isosurface Ray Tracing
definition: A two-phase algorithm for rendering isosurfaces in volumetric data on multi-core processors. Phase I traverses a coarse BONO tree to build a short, front-to-back ordered list of visible, isosurface-intersecting data blocks for each pixel (or packet). Phase II shoots rays through these lists to find the first isosurface intersection, performing trilinear interpolation and shading.
summary: Interactive High Resolution Isosurface Ray Tracing renders volumetric data by decoupling visibility culling from ray intersection using a BONO tree, differing from standard methods by relying on algorithmic list merging rather than SIMD instructions.
